description: The line plot illustrates the performance of four different methods—TACRED, TACRED-Revisit, Re-TACRED, and SemEval—in terms of Micro F1 score (%) as a function of the number of samples generated, with values plotted at K=8, K=16, K=32, and K=64. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Samples Generated,” is categorical and spans four discrete points: K=8, K=16, K=32, and K=64. The y-axis, labeled “Micro F1 (%)”, is linear and ranges from 20% to 55%, with major gridlines and tick labels at 25%, 30%, 35%, 40%, 45%, 50%, and 55%. The blue line with circle markers (TACRED) starts at approximately 22.5% at K=8, rises to ~28% at K=16, peaks at ~30.5% at K=32, and then slightly declines to ~29.5% at K=64. The orange line with triangle markers (TACRED-Revisit) begins at ~23% at K=8, increases to ~29.5% at K=16, reaches ~31% at K=32, and then drops slightly to ~30% at K=64. The green line with diamond markers (Re-TACRED) starts at ~35% at K=8, climbs to ~40.5% at K=16, peaks sharply at ~50.5% at K=32, and then decreases to ~48% at K=64. The red line with square markers (SemEval) begins at ~42% at K=8, steadily increases to ~45% at K=16, continues rising to ~47.5% at K=32, and reaches its highest point at ~51.5% at K=64. All lines show generally increasing trends with sample size, though Re-TACRED and SemEval exhibit the strongest performance, with Re-TACRED peaking at K=32 and SemEval continuing to improve through K=64.
